title: Unit changes, returning heroes, truer tags
items: Units: a Unit changes matrix like Hero and Item changes; units that share a name show what tells them apart (alt, weak, amber, model 2); removed units hide behind a switch.
Heroes and abilities Valve cut from the files before a reveal and put back now show what changed meanwhile (639 values across 47 entities) instead of reading as all-new.
Bullet speeds before August 2025 appear in the patches too (42 changes that read as engine details).
Ability upgrade texts are filled like in the game: no more "for BuffDurations" or "+DanceMoveSpeedm".

Tags: a downside the game draws red (Golden Goose Egg's damage penalty) grows as a NERF; "increased from +2 to +3" on a newly written field is a BUFF, not NEW; fields added or removed at 0 are gone; small scaling numbers keep their digits (0.0003 → 0.00035).
Home: up to 20 recent patches; Biggest changes in even rows. A build Valve shipped twice is marked (#2).
City Never Sleeps: each item's new Corrupted version (the Broker's trade) is one row listing its bonuses instead of five NEW rows — 466 new things in the patch instead of 880.
Ability cards: no "+0m" rows, and units are printed once ("+3m", not "+3m m").
The screen flash when you take damage, where a gun's bullets leave the model and trooper sound names no longer count as balance changes.

title: Hero changes filter, cleaner hero cards, no missed changes
items: Hero changes: a filter — All, Stats, Weapon, Abilities — narrows every tile and the hover card to that part of the hero; the cell itself keeps everything a patch did.
Heroes: cards are just the portrait and the name on a plate in the hero's colour; they lift on hover.

An audit of every build found changes we had missed: bullet speeds before August 2025 (18 changes), dash times before July 2025, and item stats that were removed and later restored (now two changes with their real dates instead of one on the wrong day).

title: Hero Stats at any boon, role filter, smoother scrolling
items: Hero Stats: a Boons box shows health, bullet damage, DPS, melee and resists at any number of boons; role buttons (Marksman, Assassin, Brawler, Mystic); the heatmap is a switch.
Numbers are tinted by what they are (health green, weapon orange, spirit purple); values with a history are underlined.
History tooltips: was and now in centred columns; the % uses a plain font.
Scrolling large tables and long pages is smoother (the background no longer repaints on every frame).

title: Patch calendar, richer hero changes, cleaner stat tables
items: Patches → Calendar: every year by month and day, shaded by how many game builds landed, patch days marked (named updates in gold), with the year's numbers and the monthly cadence.
Hero and item changes: tiles show how many changes a patch made; hovering opens a card with the patch, the counts and the three biggest changes.

Items and Units & Buildings tables: one table per category with only the columns it uses; items by tier; identical copies of a unit are one row (×N); Patron, Mid Boss and troopers named as in the game.
Hero Stats: pre-release heroes hidden behind a switch; the legend chips are gone.
All tables: centred cells and headers, light lines both ways, the history tooltip included.
Stat histories no longer show '11.26 → —' and '— → 11.62' when a value was briefly missing from the game files: it is one change, 11.26 → 11.62.

title: Hero and item change matrices
items: Heroes → Hero changes and Items → Item changes: every hero or item against every patch; each square is striped in the colours of what changed (buffs, nerfs, new, removed…), with switches for older patches, buff vs nerf and each tag, and a search.
Heroes: pre-release heroes are hidden until you switch them on; unreleased heroes are folded.
Patches list: the heroes hit come right after the title; the counters no longer spill into the next column.
Stat history tooltip: the date and the numbers sit on one line.

title: Interface tab, gold update names, cleaner dates
items: Patch pages: interface, sound and settings changes have their own tab 'Interface & sound', a grid of features with their names in bold; the patch notes keep the gameplay.
Notes lines the files cannot back no longer say CHANGED; a feature's name is bold.
Named updates show their name in gold instead of a star icon.
Dates use a plain font everywhere; the stat history tooltip lines its numbers up in columns.
Heroes: one grid (no 'Great for new players' row); each name plate carries the hero's colour from the game.

title: Items and heroes laid out like the game
items: Items: the game's shop — a row per tier with its price, columns Weapon, Spirit, Vitality; cards show ACTIVE and IMBUE like in the shop; hovering an item lights up its components and what it builds into. Street Brawl legendaries and removed items have their own blocks.
Heroes: tall portraits in the game's order (The Doorman under D), a 'Great for new players' row, role and complexity under each name, a pre-release ribbon and what the last patch did.

title: Tags that mean something: fixed BUFF/NERF, UP/DOWN for shared objects, readable labels
items: About 180 changes had BUFF and NERF the wrong way round: investment bonuses, Cooldown Reduction, enemy healing penalties, spread recovery. The direction is now read from the property's own name.

Troopers, guardians, walkers, camps and game rules get UP / DOWN instead of CHANGED (both teams have them); a camp's bounty, a powerup's strength and shorter respawn timers are BUFF / NERF for whoever takes them.
A field added and then tuned within one patch is NEW (it showed '— → 0.75'); tuned and then removed is DEL; a renamed field is judged like any change.
The same edit to several copies of one object (Walker in 4 versions, two crate ids) is one card: 'Walker · 4 variants'.
Tables edited row by row (souls per level, investment steps, the shotgun's pellet pattern) are one summary row with the range; the rows open on click.

Readable labels: 'Level 22: souls needed', 'Vitality investment, step 5: bonus', 'Kit: Ability 3', 'Powerup: Fire Rate (early game)', 'Sight Range NPCs', 'Spawn Interval (s)'; values like 'EHeroDevState_PreRelease' read 'Pre Release'.
Vote stickers, rich presence text, name offsets, trooper hit animations, collision hulls and soul-orb physics are no longer listed as gameplay.

City Never Sleeps: its official page is a full change list laid out as a magazine; its 195 lines (map, gameplay, The Broker, hero vote, interface, sandbox, settings and the 40 'Additional Update Notes') are now the patch notes, matched against the game files. Lore and taglines are not copied.

title: Patch titles, graded % pills, hero stats in the header
items: Patch titles show the date once; named updates (City Never Sleeps, Matchmaking Update) get a star and their name with the date beside it.
The % next to a change gets stronger colour the bigger the change: a 2% nudge is faint, a 60% swing is full colour.
Stat history tooltips no longer show an empty % box for a first value or a 0.0% step.
Hero pages: every main stat is a tile in the header, the rest under 'All stats'; the weapon's six key numbers stay visible, the rest under 'All weapon stats'; values are centred.
Tags and counters use the site's own pixel icons (arrows, star, cross, swap, gear) instead of font symbols that looked different on every device.
Build pages: a newly added hero, ability or item shows what it is (health, speed, abilities, key values) instead of hundreds of raw fields; the rest folds under 'All fields'.

title: Redesign: cards, banners, readable pixel fonts
items: New fonts: Jersey 20 for headings and names (clear pixel digits), VT323 for labels and tags, IBM Plex Sans for text.
Every change list is a set of entity cards: big icon, name, ▲▼ counters and a strip of the last 12 patches; rows with the tag, the text and old → new with a % pill.
Patch pages open with a summary: buffs / nerfs / new / removed, the heroes hit (click to jump to their card), the notes check in one line, ◀ ▶ to step between patches.
Patch notes are grouped by hero and ability with section banners; exact lines no longer repeat their numbers.
Hero pages: official notes sit inside the ability they are about; older patches fold; abilities show their last change and history; the weapon's key numbers are large.
Patches index grouped by month with follow-ups under their parent, ▲▼ counts and the heroes hit.
A smaller bonus to cooldown (-20s → -18s) is now a nerf, not a buff.
Engine plumbing rows fold into 'Technical'; a renamed field shows as one change instead of removed + added.
Hero pages: the weapon's six key numbers in one row of equal tiles; history is one panel per patch with the abilities as sub-headers; 'Only hidden' sits next to the History heading.
Item pages: the current values sit beside the history.
Heroes list: under every portrait, what the hero's last patch did (▲▼✦✕) and its date.
Small names use a plain readable font; the pixel font stays for headings and big numbers.
Patch summaries count new and removed abilities per hero too; a replaced upgrade tier shows its old and new bonuses on one muted line.
Hero Stats: every column group is labelled at its start; a fade on the right shows there are more columns; a corner notch marks values changed in the last 45 days.
Every counter on every page counts the same rows: engine plumbing no longer makes a patch look like a hero's last change.
Ability text reads like the game: 'spirit damage over time' instead of 'SpiritDPS', '+2m' instead of '+2mm', keys shown as [Move Forward].
Names Valve wrote without a gap in the localization file are read (Viscous: Splatapult; labels such as 'Bounces').
A shorter time between heal or damage ticks is a buff (Rem: Infest Heal Interval 3 → 2).
Change rows are denser and their new values line up in one column.

title: Global lines, icons everywhere, tooltips that fit, one-line table headers
items: Lines that move one stat of every hero by an amount ('Base HP reduced by 10 for all heroes', 'Bullet Cycle Time increased by 5%', 'Spirit Power scaling reduced by 7%') now cover those changes instead of leaving dozens 'hidden'.

Troopers, Guardians, Walkers, Patron, Mid Boss and neutral camps show the portraits the game itself uses; map pickups their ping icons; group rows ('All heroes (24)', game rules) a category glyph — no empty icon boxes left.
Ability cards show the in-game property icons (cooldown, duration, spirit damage…), with spirit damage in purple.
Tags: tinted chips with a colour bar; stronger fill for bigger changes.
Tooltips stay inside the screen and can be tapped on phones.
Hero Stats: short one-line headers (full name on hover); niche columns (spread, gravity, collision…) behind a Details button.
City Never Sleeps now uses its forum changelog (interface lines) and keeps a 'From the files' tab with the biggest changes.
Neutral camps and Guardians are no longer listed as troopers.
Patch notes are laid out by hero, item and ability with icons, a tag per line and highlighted old → new numbers, instead of Valve's plain text.
Labels from the game no longer show '&' instead of '&'.

title: Weapon block, grouped history, readable tags, new builds within 15 minutes
items: Hero pages: the weapon comes first as its own block with its in-game name (Abrams: Case Closed) and every gun number; abilities follow; the other stats are compact panels with the game's stat icons.
History and patch changes are grouped by ability: one header with counters, the rows below without repeating the name; a tier whose bonuses were swapped shows as one REWORK row.
Tags: smaller, readable, no duplicated percentage; availability shows ON / OFF; mechanic changes MECH.
Changes to heroes still in development are marked with a flask and a violet tint, and counted on patch pages.

Patch notes: sub-headings are recognised, lines about sound, visuals, interface, the map or the engine are marked as not part of the compared data, May 2024 lines as having no game files, lines that an edited Steam post copied from a later update point to it; unlinked note lines went from 3,716 to about 1,700.
Notes that reached the game files days later are tied to the build where they landed: the 12-06-2024 update now includes its 12-14 builds instead of a separate 'unannounced' update.
Text-change lists show names ('Afterburn · T1 description') instead of localization keys.
Hero pages drop the hero's name from note lines; abilities re-created under a new id keep their icon.
Hero Stats table: thin grid lines and centred numbers.
New game builds are picked up automatically within about 15 minutes.

title: History from June 2024, sharper hidden-change detection, new hero and patch pages
items: Game data now starts on 2024-06-06 (the predecessor tracker): 11 more early patches are checked against the files.

Hidden changes re-checked against an audit of ~1000 changes: global lines ('all ultimates +15% cooldown'), item components, tier rewrites, unit names and multi-field mechanics are now recognised as described.
Engine plumbing, Street Brawl draft weights and changes to unreleased heroes no longer count as hidden.
Updates without official numbers (City Never Sleeps) get patch notes written from the files and a list of the biggest changes.
Hero pages: key stats, stat tables with history, ability cards rebuilt from the in-game tooltip (values, spirit scaling, T1-T3 text), history as one table.
Patch pages: tabs, the files' values next to every note line, changes grouped by hero.
Icons for removed items and abilities (e.g. Tokamak) from older game files.

title: Cyclopean launches
items: Every Deadlock build since August 2024 compared field by field.
Patch pages: official notes checked against the game files — documented, described, hidden and mismatched changes.
Hero, item and unit pages with full history.
Hero stats table with the history of every cell.
